ORDER The petitioners assert that they were the owners of about 7.57 acres in S.F.Nos.324/1 and 324/2 at 184, Karumarapakkam village.
The said lands were acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (Land Acquisition Act) and compensation was paid to the petitioners.
On the basis that the said lands have not been put to use for any public purpose, after submitting joint representation dated 27.10.2024, the present writ petition has been filed.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the lands were being used for agriculture by the petitioners and that the petitioners are entitled to reconveyance thereof in view of the lands lying unutilised for a considerable period of time.
3. Mr.Abhishek Murthy, learned Government Advocate, accepts notice for respondents 1, 4 to 6.
Ms.S.Shakila Bhanu, learned standing counsel, accepts notice for the second respondent.
Mr.Krishna Ravindran, learned counsel, accepts notice for the third respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

Mr.Abhishek Murthy, learned Government Advocate, submits that the Land Acquisition Act was repealed and that the provision for reconveyance under Act 30 of 2013 is not applicable to an acquisition under the Land Acquisition Act.
5. On perusal of the affidavit, it is evident that the land acquisition proceedings were undertaken in the 1970s.
It is also clear that the petitioners have received compensation.
The said statute enables the utilisation of land not only for the stated purpose but for any other public purpose.
At this distant point of time, the request for reconveyance cannot be countenanced.
Therefore, this writ petition is dismissed without any order as to costs.
